clue.text: John having a quick sleep — 'e's a cheeky monkey

parts.note: Jack is a familiar form of the name John
a nap is a short doze
'e's is he's with the H dropped, leaving the letters E and S

explanation.surface: A man called John nods off, and someone remarks that he is a cheeky monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'e's is the cockney-style elision; only the letters E and S survive.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackanapes is an impertinent, mischievous person, originally a tame ape, so a rascal.

clue.text: A saint remembered in Cornwall only?

definitions.meaning: Saint ..., commemorated in the Cornish town of St ...
only as an adverb, meaning merely

explanation.surface: A question whether one saint is honoured solely in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: St Just is a Cornish town named after a local saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Just gives his name to St Just in Penwith; separately, the adverb means merely or simply.

clue.text: Inspect sailor ending on board

parts.note: to inspect is to check
a mate is a ship's officer, hence a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone examines a sailor whose career is finishing aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship, but it is a chessboard: the game ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkmate is the position that finishes a chess game, played out on a chessboard.

clue.text: Crime of murder finally admitted by a boy

indicators.note: something admitted by another is let inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a son is a male child, a boy

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word murder

explanation.surface: A lad confesses at last to the crime of murder.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Concoction of clay to limit a bit of a cough? Not proper science

indicators.note: to limit something is to confine it, so the shuffled letters close around the cough
a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of clay are stirred up

parts.note: hem is a short clearing of the throat, a little cough

explanation.surface: Someone mixes up clay to stop a cough, which is hardly real science.
explanation.walkthrough: The cough remedy picture hides the device: 'Concoction of' makes ALCY, which 'to limit' closes around the throat-clearing sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemy, the medieval quest to turn base metals into gold, is a pseudoscience rather than true chemistry.

clue.text: What upsets me about a lord possibly is his rank

indicators.note: something that upsets is thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A complaint that a nobleman's title is what really annoys the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' jumbles ME, A and LORD; 'about' and 'possibly' only link, with 'possibly' hinting that a lord might be an earl.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the title and status held by an earl, a peer of the realm.

clue.text: Work in shop usefully

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words shop usefully

explanation.surface: Someone is doing helpful work in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for a work, used for a musical composition or piece of writing.

clue.text: Chaplain who may have accommodation with the engineers?

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or living quarters
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an army chaplain might share lodgings with the sappers.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the military nickname for a forces clergyman.

clue.text: Wear this casually in the street?

definitions.text: Wear this casually in the street?

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters between the two letters for street
done casually means without order, so the letters of wear this are scattered

explanation.surface: A suggestion for informal clothing to put on when out walking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casually' jumbles WEAR THIS to WEATSHIR, and 'in' sets that between S and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshirt is a loose cotton jersey, the kind of informal top worn about town.

clue.text: Terrible pride? That is universal thing to bring you to your knees

definitions.text: thing to bring you to your knees

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters of pride are mangled

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
U is the film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: Pride is a dreadful sin, and that humbles everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A prie-dieu is a prayer desk with a low ledge for kneeling.

clue.text: Son follows domestic animals around making short journeys

indicators.note: turned around means the word pets is read backwards

parts.note: pets are animals kept in the home

explanation.surface: A boy trails the household pets as they make little trips about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' gives STEP, and 'follows' places the son's letter last; 'making' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Steps are single paces, so a step is the briefest walk from one spot to another.

clue.text: One may hold film showing vehicle by strip of land

parts.note: a cart is a simple wheeled vehicle
a ridge is a long narrow raised strip of ground

explanation.surface: A truck is pictured parked beside a narrow stretch of countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is a sealed case loaded with camera film, ink or ammunition.

clue.text: He's a kind to look unconventional

definitions.text: He's a kind to look unconventional

indicators.note: unconventional means departing from the norm, so the letters of he's a kind are reordered

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain man's type has a way of looking odd.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive-looking 's is a letter here, part of the eight letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinhead is a youth with a shaved scalp, a subculture known for its striking look.

clue.text: Choose the Spanish form of therapy

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine word for the
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: Someone is picking the Spanish version of a medical treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to pick, typically by voting.

clue.text: I do a search here and there to find solid shapes

indicators.note: here and there means scattered about, so the letters of i do a search are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hunts all over the place to track down some three-dimensional figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Icosahedra are polyhedra with twenty faces, geometric solids.

clue.text: An organisation like the salvation army is cautious about it

definitions.text: An organisation like the salvation army

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: chary means wary or careful

explanation.surface: A remark that a famous religious relief group is wary about something.
explanation.walkthrough: The Salvation Army is a Christian church and relief body; 'about' means going round here, not concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salvation Army is a registered body raising money and giving aid, a benevolent nonprofit.

clue.text: Cheeky and inconsiderate? That's not right

indicators.note: not says the letter for right is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: imprudent means rash or not thinking ahead

explanation.surface: A question whether being cheeky and thoughtless is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent means insolent or disrespectful, showing nerve towards others.

clue.text: "Girly" mum — one very attractive lady

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
I is the Roman numeral for one
a dish is slang for a gorgeous person

explanation.surface: A mother described as girlish is a real stunner.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidish means like a young unmarried woman, so girlish.

clue.text: Legal document could show rent due in

indicators.note: could show suggests the letters might be rearranged to reveal another word

explanation.surface: A tenancy paper might reveal that rent is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal contract, classically binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Football player ultimately joyless, one reduced to tears

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of joyless

parts.note: a weeper is someone who cries

explanation.surface: A footballer, finally miserable, ends up crying.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeper is a defender who plays behind the back line in soccer.

clue.text: Make good support with naturally occurring material

parts.note: a rest is a prop or support
ore is a mineral mined from the earth

explanation.surface: Repairing something with a brace made of natural stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore is to repair or return something to its former condition.

clue.text: One who has made an establishment collapse

definitions.text: One who has made an establishment
definitions.meaning: a person who set up a firm, school or similar
to give way or sink, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Someone who built a business sees it fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A founder starts an institution; as a verb, to founder is to sink or fail.

clue.text: Less exciting compliment

definitions.meaning: the comparative of flat, meaning more dull
a verb here, to praise someone

explanation.surface: Praise that is rather dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatter is the comparative of flat, meaning duller; as a verb it means to praise insincerely.

clue.text: Listened to end of lecture — difficult to grasp it

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold, so the first word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: hard means difficult

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of lecture

explanation.surface: A student attends the close of a talk that is tough to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grasp' puts E inside HARD; 'it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Heard is the past participle of hear, so attended to by ear.

clue.text: What you might have found in equestrian village?

definitions.text: What you might have found in equestrian village?

indicators.note: found in says the letters are discovered inside the words equestrian village

explanation.surface: A question about what a horsey hamlet might contain.
explanation.walkthrough: A horse-loving village would have a blacksmith's forge, and so this tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the iron block a farrier hammers horseshoes on.

clue.text: Namely, an object seen as detrimental

parts.note: sc. is the abbreviation of scilicet, Latin for namely
an as the indefinite article, written as the letter A
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A thing is described as harmful.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathing means harshly critical, so damaging or hurtful.

clue.text: Comic writer

definitions.meaning: a comedian, Oliver of Laurel and ...
a novelist, Thomas of Tess of the d'Urbervilles

explanation.surface: A humorous author.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Hardy was the comic partner of Stan Laurel; Thomas Hardy was the novelist of Wessex.

clue.text: A band's hit?

definitions.meaning: a strip of material, as worn round the waist

explanation.surface: A question whether some pop group had a chart success.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap round the waist is a girdle or strip; as a verb it means to strike hard.

clue.text: Sofa making 7 on TV look sloppy

indicators.note: to look sloppy is to be untidy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: 7 refers to the answer to 7 down, a chaplain

explanation.surface: A settee makes a TV preacher appear scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look sloppy' jumbles the letters of 7-down, PADRE, with ON and TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A davenport is a large upholstered couch in American usage, and a writing desk in British use.

clue.text: The way the cause of anything is mentioned

indicators.note: is mentioned signals that the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: the root of a problem is its source or origin

explanation.surface: A remark about how the origin of something gets discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a path or course taken.

clue.text: Competent third man from what we hear

indicators.note: from what we hear signals that the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: Abel, son of Adam and Eve, was the third man in the Bible after Adam and Cain

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that the third man is skilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third man' suggests the film or a cricket position, but it is the Bible's third human.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable or skilled.

clue.text: Payment freed many possibly before time

indicators.note: before puts the shuffled letters ahead of the letter for time
possibly suggests another arrangement of the letters of freed many

explanation.surface: A settlement released numerous people ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Defrayment is the act of meeting a cost, settling the bill.
